title: Review: Chemical signalling; Neural signalling; Integration of body systems

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Neuromuscular junction
items.clue: The synapse between a motor neuron and a skeletal muscle fibre.

items.label: Cell body
items.clue: The part of a neuron that contains the nucleus and most of the cytoplasm.

items.label: Baroreceptor
items.clue: A stretch receptor in the walls of the aorta and the carotid arteries that monitors blood pressure.

items.label: Sensory neuron
items.clue: A neuron that conveys messages, as nerve impulses, from receptor cells to the central nervous system.

questions.stem: A motor neuron has its cell body in the spinal cord and a single fibre about 1 m long that reaches a muscle in the foot. What is this fibre?

options.text: One of the neuron's several axons, each of which reaches a different muscle in the leg.
An axon: a single long fibre along which impulses are conducted away from the cell body.
A nerve, because a fibre this long must be made of many neurons joined end to end.
A connecting fibre that links the neuron to the muscle but is not part of the neuron itself.

questions.stem: Why is a nerve impulse described as an electrical signal?

options.text: It consists of electrons flowing along the inside of the fibre, in the same way as a current in a metal wire.
It consists of positively charged ions moving across the membrane, which changes the membrane potential.
It consists of neurotransmitter molecules travelling along the fibre and carrying their electrical charge with them.
It consists of sodium ions flowing along the whole length of the fibre from one end of it to the other.

questions.stem: Why can a signal pass in only one direction across a synapse?

options.text: Electric current can only cross the cleft from the more positive presynaptic membrane to the more negative postsynaptic one.
Calcium ions can only diffuse across the cleft from the presynaptic side, because that is where they are concentrated.
Carrier proteins in the cleft actively transport the neurotransmitter towards the postsynaptic membrane only.
Only the presynaptic neuron stores neurotransmitter in vesicles, and only the postsynaptic membrane has receptors for it.

questions.stem: What is the role of calcium ions in the release of neurotransmitter from a presynaptic neuron?

options.text: Depolarization of the presynaptic membrane opens calcium channels; calcium ions enter and signal vesicles to fuse with the membrane.
Calcium ions are released from the presynaptic neuron and diffuse across the cleft, where they then depolarize the postsynaptic membrane.
Calcium ions have no role, because neurotransmitter simply diffuses out through the presynaptic membrane when an impulse arrives.
Calcium ions provide the energy for carrier proteins to pump the neurotransmitter across the synaptic cleft to its postsynaptic receptors.

questions.stem: How does acetylcholine generate an excitatory postsynaptic potential?

options.text: It diffuses across the cleft and enters the postsynaptic cell, where it depolarizes the membrane from the inside.
It is actively transported across the cleft by carrier proteins, which use ATP to push it into the postsynaptic cell.
It diffuses across the cleft and binds to transmembrane receptors, opening channels through which sodium ions enter the postsynaptic cell.
It diffuses across the cleft and binds to receptors, opening channels through which potassium ions enter the postsynaptic cell.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes what is meant by integration in a living system?

options.text: Coordination of the component parts so that together they perform an overall function that none performs alone.
Each component part performs its own function independently, so the parts do not need to interact.
A single dominant part carries out the overall function while the other parts play no role in it.
Coordination is achieved only by conscious decisions, so it applies only to organisms with a brain.

questions.stem: Which statement about the spinal cord and unconscious processes is correct?

options.text: The spinal cord only conducts impulses between the body and the brain, so every kind of integration must take place in the brain itself.
The spinal cord integrates some unconscious responses, receiving sensory input and sending motor output without the brain deciding.
Every unconscious process is integrated in the spinal cord, because everything that the brain does is conscious.
Reflexes are called unconscious only because the brain makes the decision too quickly for us to be aware of doing so.

questions.stem: What is the function of sensory neurons?

options.text: They carry impulses out from the central nervous system to the receptors that must then respond.
They detect every stimulus themselves, so the body needs no separate receptor cells.
They convey impulses from receptor cells to the spinal cord and the cerebral hemispheres.
They are the nerves that connect each sense organ to the brain, each made of one long fibre.

questions.explanation: Sensory neurons convey messages from receptor cells to the central nervous system, providing the input to the spinal cord and cerebral hemispheres.

questions.stem: Which statement about the relationship between a nerve and a neuron is correct?

options.text: A nerve and a neuron are the same structure; nerve is simply the word used for a neuron long enough to be seen unaided.
A nerve is a bundle of nerve fibres from many neurons and usually contains fibres of both sensory and motor neurons.
A nerve contains the fibres of many neurons, but all the fibres in any one nerve are either sensory or motor.
A nerve is a group of neurons wrapped together in a single myelin sheath, which acts as its protective sheath.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the role of the cerebellum in the control of body movements?

options.text: It coordinates the contraction of skeletal muscles so that movements are smooth and accurate, and it maintains balance.
It initiates voluntary movements by deciding which skeletal muscles should contract and at what moment.
It has no role in balance, which is maintained entirely by the semicircular canals within the inner ear.
It controls involuntary movements such as the heartbeat and breathing rather than any of the skeletal muscles.

questions.stem: Which statement describes how the hypothalamus and the pituitary gland control the endocrine system?

options.text: The hypothalamus controls the pituitary gland, which secretes hormones that act on body tissues or that control other endocrine glands.
The pituitary gland controls the other endocrine glands by itself; the hypothalamus is part of the nervous system and plays no role.
The hypothalamus controls the pituitary gland by nerve impulses only, because the hypothalamus cannot secrete any hormones.
Each endocrine gland monitors the blood and secretes its hormone independently, so no gland controls any other gland.

questions.stem: Electrodes inside and outside an axon show that the inside briefly becomes positive relative to the outside as an impulse passes. What causes this change?

options.text: Potassium ions move into the axon across the membrane at that point.
Electrons move out of the axon along the inner surface of its membrane.
Sodium ions move into the axon across the membrane at that point.
Sodium ions arriving from further back along the axon accumulate at that point.

questions.explanation: During an action potential sodium ions diffuse into the axon through the membrane, adding positive charge inside so that the membrane potential briefly reverses to positive. The impulse is electrical because of this movement of positively charged ions.

questions.stem: How does a steroid hormone such as testosterone change the expression of genes in a target cell?

options.text: It diffuses through the membrane into the nucleus and binds directly to the DNA at the start of the genes it switches on.
It binds a receptor in the plasma membrane, and this receptor then detaches and travels to the nucleus to bind the DNA.
It is pumped across the membrane by a transport protein, since steroids cannot cross the bilayer, and then activates a receptor inside.
It enters the cell and activates a receptor inside it, which binds specific DNA sequences to promote transcription.

questions.stem: What is the effect of progesterone on the cells of the endometrium?

options.text: It causes the endometrium to break down and be shed, which is why menstruation happens while progesterone is being secreted.
It binds directly to the DNA of the endometrial cells and switches on the genes that cause growth of the lining.
It maintains and thickens the endometrium, making its glands secrete and increasing its blood supply for implantation.
It binds to receptors on the surface of endometrial cells and raises cAMP inside them, which makes the lining grow much thicker.

questions.stem: How do local currents propagate an action potential along an axon?

options.text: Sodium ions that entered at the start travel along the whole axon to its end, carrying the depolarization with them.
Sodium ions that entered diffuse to the next region and depolarize it fully, so no voltage-gated channels are needed there.
Electrons released when the sodium channels open flow along the inside of the axon, depolarizing the whole length at once.
Sodium ions that entered diffuse along the inside of the axon to the next region, bringing it to threshold so its sodium channels open.

questions.stem: An oscilloscope trace covering 60 ms shows 15 action potentials. What is the frequency of impulses?

options.text: 0.25 impulses per second
4 impulses per second
250 impulses per second
15 impulses per second

questions.explanation: 60 ms is 0.060 s, so the frequency is 15 ÷ 0.060 = 250 impulses per second. The number of impulses per second is measured from a trace by counting the spikes and dividing by the time covered, in seconds.

questions.stem: Which statement explains saltatory conduction in a myelinated nerve fibre?

options.text: Ion channels and pumps are clustered at the nodes of Ranvier, so action potentials occur only at the nodes and the impulse passes from node to node.
The myelin sheath conducts the electrical current along the fibre, so the impulse travels through the myelin between the nodes.
Action potentials occur along the entire membrane of the fibre, but the myelin makes each of them develop more quickly.
The nodes of Ranvier are gaps in the insulation where the impulse leaks out, so each node slows the impulse slightly.

questions.stem: How do neonicotinoid pesticides block synaptic transmission in insects?

options.text: They block the reuptake of acetylcholine into the presynaptic neuron, so the insect's synapses soon run out of neurotransmitter.
They inhibit the enzyme acetylcholinesterase in the cleft, so acetylcholine is not broken down at all after it has been released.
They prevent calcium ions from crossing the synaptic cleft, so the postsynaptic membrane is not depolarized at all.
They bind to acetylcholine receptors at the insect's synapses, so acetylcholine can no longer transmit signals across them.
